what_changed.text: A broad stock sell-off has left the market 17% below its peak. This is the change most likely to come up, because Daniel is about to stop work.
After the sell-off, Ruth and Daniel say they want a more conservative mix in their portfolio.
Ten-year Treasury yields have climbed to 4.80%.
One-year bank CDs are paying about 4.60% a year.
An immediate income annuity for a new retiree pays out about 6.80% of the premium a year.
A new law moves the start of required minimum distributions to age 75.

why_it_matters.text: The household wants a steady income floor and fears a drop right after Daniel retires. A 17% market decline puts that fear in front of them now.
Their stated wish for a more conservative mix gives you a clear opening to discuss what they want their income floor to look like.
Ten-year Treasury yields at 4.80% and one-year CDs at about 4.60% are relevant to the CDs they already hold with us. They also frame how the household compares income options.
The RMD start age moving to 75 may change when the rollover IRA has to pay out. That affects how you plan withdrawals across their accounts.

likely_questions.text: Ruth or Daniel may ask: 'Should we wait to retire because the market is down 17%?' The facts do not cover their spending needs or savings, so this needs follow-up.

They may ask how a CD at about 4.60% compares with an income annuity paying about 6.80% of premium a year. The facts give the rates but not the terms, features or how the two differ, so the comparison needs follow-up.

They may ask when they must start taking money from the rollover IRA. The new law sets the start age at 75. Their exact ages and any effect on their plan are not in the facts, so that needs follow-up.

talking_points.text: Open with the 17% drop and ask how it has affected Ruth and Daniel's comfort with their current mix.
Ask what 'more conservative' means to them in practice, and how much steady income they want each month.
Walk through the current rate picture: 4.80% on ten-year Treasuries, about 4.60% on one-year CDs, and about 6.80% of premium a year on an immediate income annuity for a new retiree.
Explain the new RMD start age of 75 and ask how it fits their plan for the rollover IRA.

watch_outs.text: The rate facts are dated January and February 2026 and the market fact is dated March 2026. Confirm current figures before quoting them to the client.
The annuity payout figure is a general rate for a new retiree, not a quote for Ruth and Daniel. Do not present it as their payout.
The facts do not include account balances, spending needs, Social Security or exact ages. Get these before the meeting or ask during it.
